cards.front: Recall a key point about Nouns & Declensions
cards.back: Latin nouns change their endings to show their grammatical function in a sentence; this system is called declension.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nouns & Declensions
cards.back: There are five declensions, each with a characteristic vowel in the stem: 1st (a-stem), 2nd (o-stem), 3rd (consonant/i-stem), 4th (u-stem), 5th (e-stem).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nouns & Declensions
cards.back: Every Latin noun has a gender: masculine, feminine, or neuter. Gender must be learned with each noun and does not always match natural sex.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nouns & Declensions
cards.back: First declension nouns are mostly feminine (e.g. puella, villa, familia). Exceptions like nauta and agricola are masculine.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nouns & Declensions
cards.back: Second declension nouns are mostly masculine (ending -us) or neuter (ending -um). Notable feminine exceptions include humus and vilicus.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nouns & Declensions
cards.back: Third declension is the largest and most varied group; it contains nouns of all three genders and has both consonant stems and i-stems.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nouns & Declensions
cards.back: The stem of a noun is found by removing the ending from the genitive singular and adding the neuter -ia: e.g. rex, regis → stem reg-.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nouns & Declensions
cards.back: Fourth declension nouns are mostly masculine (e.g. adventus, spiritus) with a few neuter (e.g. cornu, genu).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nouns & Declensions
cards.back: Fifth declension nouns are almost all feminine (e.g. res, dies) and few in number. Dies can be masculine when meaning a set date.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Nouns & Declensions
cards.back: Neuter nouns follow the rule: the nominative and accusative forms are identical in both singular and plural, and the plural nominative/accusative ends in -a.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse latin exam tips — nouns & declensions?
cards.back: 1. For Nouns & Declensions, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Nouns & Declensions, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
Explain the Latin declension system, using examples from at least three declensions to show how case endings indicate grammatical function. (6 marks)
